purpose: Preserve national cost-pressure context for essential household lanes without treating CPI as a complete household purchasing-power measure.
scope: United States national CPI context, January-July 2026
governing_rule: These observations describe national price-index movement only. They may support essential-cost context, but cannot by themselves establish delivered household bill changes, household burden, unmet need, or cross-category causation.
bounded_findings: Water/sewer, shelter/rent, and household-insurance price indexes were all above their year-earlier levels in March 2026, so these essential or quasi-required household costs were not neutral background categories during the shipping/energy shock.
Water/sewer maintenance remained about 5 percent above year-earlier levels by July, while shelter and rent remained above year-earlier levels as well.
These national price indexes do not measure local regulated charges, contracted rates, household usage, income share, arrears, or actual delivered bills.

next_required_evidence: delivered bill or tariff data where regulated charges matter
service quantity or unmet-need indicators where available
